results.corrected_claim: iOS 27 adds two modifiers. (1) `nonisolated func swipeActions(edge: HorizontalEdge = .trailing, allowsFullSwipe: Bool = true, @ContentBuilder content: () -> some View, onPresentationChanged: @escaping (Bool) -> Void) -> some View`. Abstract: "Adds custom swipe actions to a row in a list or container, notifying you when the actions are revealed or dismissed." (2) `nonisolated func swipeActionsContainer() -> some View`. Abstract: "Coordinates swipe action dismissal and mutual exclusion across rows in a container." Its discussion says: "Use swipeActionsContainer() when building custom row-based layouts that use ScrollView, LazyVStack, or similar containers." and "Applying this modifier to a List is a no-op, since List already provides this coordination." Both are introduced in iOS 27.0, iPadOS 27.0, Mac Catalyst 27.0, macOS 27.0, visionOS 27.0 and watchOS 27.0. Neither is available on tvOS, and neither is beta or deprecated.
results.notes: Source type: apple-doc. Checked swipeactionscontainer().json and swipeactions(edge:allowsfullswipe:content:onpresentationchanged:).json; both declarations match the finding verbatim. The SwiftUI Updates page (June 2026, General) also says: "Add custom swipe actions to views in containers such as scroll views, stacks, grids, or custom layouts using swipeActions(edge:allowsFullSwipe:content:onPresentationChanged:) and swipeActionsContainer()." Nuance: Apple's swipeActionsContainer example puts the existing iOS 15 `.swipeActions { }` (edge:allowsFullSwipe:content:) on rows inside ScrollView/LazyVStack. That older modifier's own page still says "Adds custom swipe actions to a row in a list." and has no iOS 27 note. Because swipeActionsContainer() is 27.0-only, using swipe actions outside List needs `if #available(iOS 27, *)` gating in a skill that targets iOS 26+. Applying it to card stacks is the finder's own (reasonable) application; Apple's wording is "row-based layouts".

results.corrected_claim: The six new overload families exist and are listed under SwiftUI Updates, June 2026 (Alerts and confirmation dialogs): alert(_:item:actions:), alert(error:actions:), alert(_:item:actions:message:), alert(error:actions:message:), confirmationDialog(_:item:titleVisibility:actions:) and confirmationDialog(_:item:titleVisibility:actions:message:). The iOS 27 release notes (SwiftUI > New Features) say verbatim: "The new data item or error object based alert and confirmationDialog modifiers can now be used by projects targeting iOS 15.0, macOS 12.0, tvOS 15.0, watchOS 8.0, and visionOS 1.0. (179388848)". The quoted Text-title declaration is verbatim correct. Back-deployment is NOT uniform across overloads, though: (a) The Text, LocalizedStringKey and StringProtocol title overloads, and the error overloads constrained `where E : LocalizedError`, are `@export(implementation)` and show iOS/iPadOS/Mac Catalyst/tvOS 15.0, macOS 12.0, visionOS 1.0 and watchOS 8.0. (b) The LocalizedStringResource-title overloads (e.g. alert(_:item:actions:)-4qsee and confirmationDialog(_:item:titleVisibility:actions:)-b3zs) show iOS 16.0, macOS 13.0, tvOS 16.0, watchOS 9.0 and visionOS 1.0. (c) alert(error:actions:)-dxc7 `nonisolated func alert<E, A>(error: Binding<E?>, @ContentBuilder actions: () -> A) -> some View where E : Error, A : View` and alert(error:actions:message:)-27vbr (where E : Error) have NO @export(implementation) and are 27.0 on iOS, iPadOS, Mac Catalyst, macOS, tvOS, visionOS and watchOS. For those, the title falls back to localizedDescription when the error is not a LocalizedError.
results.notes: Source type: apple-doc + apple-other (release notes). Pages checked: alert(_:item:actions:) plus -28uwn, -4pwxo and -4qsee; alert(_:item:actions:message:); alert(error:actions:) plus -dxc7; alert(error:actions:message:) plus -27vbr; confirmationDialog(_:item:titleVisibility:actions:) plus -b3zs; confirmationDialog(_:item:titleVisibility:actions:message:). The release-note quote was confirmed by two separate fetches. Practical impact: on an iOS 26 deployment target, `alert(error: $err)` with a plain Error type (not LocalizedError) resolves to the iOS 27-only overload and needs #available. "Requires the Xcode 27 SDK" is an inference (the symbols ship only in the 27 SDKs); Apple does not say it verbatim.

results.corrected_claim: The release-note text is real and quoted correctly. It sits under SwiftUI > Resolved Issues as: "Fixed: Certain control-related view modifiers unexpectedly affect sheet and popover content. In apps built with the 27.0 SDKs, the controlSize, buttonSizing, buttonRepeatBehavior, menuIndicatorVisibility, and ButtonBorderShape environment values are now reset to their default values in sheets and popovers. (167448274)". So these values, when set on a presenting view, no longer flow into sheet or popover content; set them inside the presented content. However, the finding's description of the skill is not supported. Every `.controlSize` / `.buttonBorderShape` use in the skill is attached directly to the Button itself: patterns/glass-tab-bar.md:63, glass-floating-toolbar.md:47, glass-card-stack.md:69, references/01-api-reference.md:264-292, 03-design-tokens.md:153-154 (recipes chained on the button), 04-motion-and-interaction.md:67, 05-accessibility.md:111/157, and the examples. None of them sits on a parent that presents a sheet. patterns/glass-modal-sheet.md has no controlSize or buttonBorderShape at all, and the examples contain no .sheet or .popover. This is a worthwhile preventive gotcha to add under glass-modal-sheet.md 'Gotchas' (line 95), not a fix for existing broken guidance.

results.corrected_claim: The iOS & iPadOS 27 release notes (SwiftUI > New Features) say verbatim: "In apps built with the iOS 27.0 and iPadOS 27.0 SDKs, a TabView enforces that its selection is set to a visible tab. TabView might crash when its selection is set to a hidden or otherwise unavailable tab. (164516837)". The skill's tab-bar Gotchas (patterns/glass-tab-bar.md lines 83-87) cover only role: .search, tabBarMinimizeBehavior and tabViewBottomAccessory, and say nothing about selection validity.
results.notes: Source type: apple-other (release notes; verbatim text consistent across two fetches). Context: the skill's own TabView sample has no `selection:` binding, so the pattern as written is not affected. The gotcha matters when a reader adds `TabView(selection:)` together with hidden or conditionally unavailable tabs; the selection must always point to a visible tab when building with the 27 SDK.

results.corrected_claim: WWDC26 session 269 'What's new in SwiftUI' contains these sentences verbatim. "When I build and run our app, the Liquid Glass design automatically takes on its updated appearance. Apps gain this look without having to change a single line of code!" "Liquid Glass has a refined look and automatically responds to the new Liquid Glass slider to adjust its tint." "On macOS, like on iOS, you can mark Liquid Glass custom elements as \"interactive\" so they respond more fluidly to user's clicks." "...our iPad app automatically takes on a distinct appearance when inactive, with the icons and text dimming to reinforce which window is active". The session also says: "Our custom account button in the sidebar dims along with the rest of the tab labels, using the appearsActive environment value to conditionally reduce the button's opacity when the window isn't active." Its sample is `@Environment(\.appearsActive) private var appearsActive` with `.opacity(appearsActive ? 1 : 0.5)`. The appearsActive declaration is `@backDeployed(before: macOS 15.0) var appearsActive: Bool { get set }`: iOS/iPadOS/Mac Catalyst/tvOS 18.0, macOS 10.15, visionOS 2.0, watchOS 11.0. I found no SwiftUI API that exposes the user's Liquid Glass tint/slider preference.
results.notes: Source type: apple-video (session page with transcript) + apple-doc. Caveat: the appearsActive doc page has not been updated. It still says "On all other platforms, this value is always `true`." and is bridged to UITraitCollection.activeAppearance, which conflicts with the iPad behaviour shown in the session. Treat the session as the newer source. Negative check for a tint-preference API: Glass members are only interactive(_:), tint(_:), clear, identity and regular (type introduced in 26.0). EnvironmentValues (both halves of the page) has no glass/liquid/tint-preference member, only accessibilityReduceTransparency, appearsActive, backgroundMaterial, materialActiveAppearance and colorSchemeContrast. The SwiftUI Updates June/September 2026 sections list no Liquid Glass appearance API. The "(built with Xcode 27)" condition is inferred from "When I build and run our app"; the session does not state the SDK requirement explicitly. The SKILL.md 'Mental model' text (line 95) is version-neutral, but the skill as a whole is scoped to iOS 26 and does not mention these iOS 27 appearance changes.

results.corrected_claim: The iOS & iPadOS 27 release notes (SwiftUI > New Features) say verbatim: "The menu bar on iPadOS 27.0 and macOS 27.0, as well as context menus on macOS 27.0, present a reduced set of menu item images. By default, SwiftUI now hides all menu item symbol images in most contexts, while non-symbol images remain visible. Review the updated Human Interface Guidelines to determine which menu items in your app should still display images. Use the labelStyle(_:) view modifier with the .titleAndIcon style to indicate that a menu item Label’s icon should always be shown — such as when the menu item represents an object or a concept rather than an action. SwiftUI continues to automatically provide default visible menu item images for certain common system-wide menu items, such as Settings, Share, and Print. (170480710)"
